models_evaluated: previously developed deep learning model for nasogastric tube verification

links.outcome: Performance of previously developed NG tube model on local hospital radiographs against expert reference standard
links.effect: Correctly classified 129 of 135 cases; sensitivity 96.1%, specificity 85.7% (95% CI 42.2-97.7%), PPV 99.2%, NPV 54.5%; AUROC 0.970; unstable performance for incomplete placements (n=6).
links.quote: The DL model performed well in identifying correctly positioned NG tubes but demonstrated limited and unstable performance for detecting incomplete placements.

links.outcome: Model detection of incomplete/malpositioned NG tube placements that would be missed if AI classification is relied on
links.effect: NPV 54.5% (95% CI 25.4-80.8%) and specificity 85.7% (95% CI 42.2-97.7%); only 6 incomplete cases, PRC AUC 0.727, with substantial uncertainty; authors call for mandatory physician oversight.
links.quote: Given the safety implications of misclassification, the model should be used only as an assistive tool with mandatory physician oversight.

screen.reason: The study retrospectively evaluates an existing deep learning model on a single-center dataset for nasogastric tube verification (external validation/failure analysis) without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
